card.statement:
Let us give an example of the induction of irreducible components. Let us consider the $A_{2}$ -quiver with $\dim V=(1,2)$, $\dim W=(1,2)$. We have an irreducible component $Y$ with $\varepsilon_{2}(Y)=1$, which is obtained from ${\mathfrak{L}}(V^{\prime},W)$ with $\dim V^{\prime}=(1,0)$, which is a single point. Nonzero maps in $Y$ are

$\begin{CD}V_{1}={\mathbb{C}}@

We can normalize $J_{1}=1$ by $\operatorname{GL}(V_{1})$, then we see that $Y$ is $\mathbb{C}P^{2}$ as $B_{1,2}\oplus J_{2}$ defines $2$ -dimensional subspace in $V_{1}\oplus W_{2}={\mathbb{C}}^{3}$.

Let us consider $\varepsilon_{1}(Y)$. For generic $[B,I,J]\in Y$, we have $B_{1,2}\neq 0$, hence $\varepsilon_{1}(Y)=0$. We add $1$ -dimensional space at the vertex $1$, and consider the irreducible component $Y^{\prime\prime}$ of ${\mathfrak{L}}(V^{\prime\prime},W)$ with $\dim V^{\prime\prime}=(2,2)$. Over $[B,I,J]\in Y$, it is given by a $1$ -dimensional subspace in the middle cohomology of the complex

${\mathbb{C}}=V_{1}\xrightarrow{0\oplus J_{1}}V_{2}\oplus W_{1}={\mathbb{C}}^{2}\oplus{\mathbb{C}}\xrightarrow{(B_{1,2},0)}V_{1}={\mathbb{C}}.$

If $B_{1,2}\neq 0$, the middle cohomology is $1$ -dimensional, hence the choice of a $1$ -dimensional subspace is unique. But note that there is a point $B_{1,2}=0$ in $Y$. Then the middle cohomology group is $2$ -dimensional, hence we have choices parametrized by $\mathbb{C}P^{1}$. This shows that $Y^{\prime\prime}$ is the blowup of $Y=\mathbb{C}P^{2}$ at the point $B_{1,2}=0$. It also gives an example where $\dim\operatorname{Hom}((B,I,J),S_{i})$ jumps at a special point in an irreducible component.
card.label: Example 18

paper.title: Introduction to quiver varieties -- for ring and representation theoriests
paper.abstract: We review the definition of quiver varieties and their relation to representation theory of Kac-Moody Lie algebras. Target readers are ring and representation theorists. We emphasize important roles of first extension groups of the preprojective algebra associated with a quiver.
